summary: Duplicates observed for function-calls after HTTP/2 stream reset due to proxy header truncation and session-scoped idempotency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external webhook invocations triggered by function-calls after an HTTP/2 RST_STREAM event. The customer uses TS SDK in their front-end to stream tokens and a Go worker to confirm tool executions. They observed the same function being executed twice (two downstream webhook POSTs) for a single user action.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream actions (webhook POST) causing double billing and incorrect user-facing state (duplicate emails/orders).
- Reproducible for specific sessions when underlying connection experiences a stream reset under proxy.

Environment details provided by customer:
- Frontend: ts-sdk v2.3.1, node 18, using streaming chat + function-calling.
- Worker: go-sdk v0.9.2 performing remote webhook POSTs upon function call confirmation.
- Backend: python ingestion service (python-sdk v1.14.0) that sometimes replays events after reconnect.
- Edge: Customer runs traffic through an HTTP/2 terminating proxy (Fastly-like CDN) that multiplexes requests and enforces header length limits (reportedly 16 bytes on a particular header).

Customer-observed symptoms:
- Two webhook deliveries within 2-5s for a single user prompt.
- SDK logs show: first stream reset (RST_STREAM) then immediate retry, second stream contains a different trace id but same session id.
- The idempotency header the customer adds (X-Idempotency-Key) appears truncated in upstream request logs.

Request from customer: explanation of root cause, recommended mitigations, and SDK config changes to avoid duplicates.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use TS SDK streaming chat with a function described in the model manifest.
2) Ensure requests pass through an HTTP/2 multiplexing proxy that truncates headers >16 bytes.
3) Send a prompt that triggers the function-calling path and force a stream reset (simulate RST_STREAM).
4) Observe worker logs: two POSTs to the external webhook for the same logical function invocation.

Notes: The customer supplied a minimal reproduction where toggling the proxy header length limit to >64 bytes stops the duplication.
logs:
[frontend] ts-sdk v2.3.1 streaming: send chunk (id=abc123, idempotency=X-Id-9a2f3c4d5e6f7g8)
[edge-proxy] received headers: x-idempotency-key=9a2f3c4d
[frontend] connection RST_STREAM (code=2)
[frontend] retry: re-open stream, send chunk (id=abc123, idempotency=X-Id-9a2f3c4d5e6f7g8)
[go-worker] function-confirmation received: invocation_id=abc123, idempotency_hdr=9a2f3c4d -> POST /webhook -> 200
[go-worker] duplicate confirmation: invocation_id=abc123-2, idempotency_hdr=9a2f3c4d -> POST /webhook -> 200

Customer supplied raw proxy capture showing header trimmed to first 8 chars. The SDK-level idempotency key appears consistent on the client side but changes after proxying.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Support):
- Reproduced with internal proxy that enforces 16-byte header max; when header truncated, server-side dedup logic cannot correlate the two attempts.
- Observed that front-end TS SDK stores an 'session' idempotency token when streaming, which is reused across stream reconnections for convenience. This pattern works when the idempotency key is preserved end-to-end, but fails when intermediary proxies mutate/truncate headers.

Hypothesis: A combination of factors causes duplicates:
- SDK session-scoped idempotency (reusing the same key across retries and multiplexed streams).
- HTTP/2 proxy header truncation/normalization causing dedup mismatch between initial and retried requests.
- RST_STREAM triggers immediate client retry with same session key, but downstream received header differs (truncated) so server treats retry as new invocation.

SDK audit:
- python-sdk v1.14.0: uses per-request idempotency if user sets explicit header; session-scoped behavior exists behind streaming convenience APIs.
- ts-sdk v2.3.1: streaming convenience path reuses session token and does not regenerate per-request UUID on reconnect.
- go-sdk v0.9.2: confirm worker uses whatever idempotency header it sees from the request to dedupe outbound webhooks (no additional server-side sequencer).

Edge findings:
- Proxy reported header length limit and lower-case normalization. Proxy also reuses underlying connection and may coalesce headers in edge cases.

Action taken so far:
- Asked customer for packet capture and request traces (provided).
- Reproduced locally with simple Fastly-like proxy and confirmed duplication scenario.
- Opened internal engineering task to adjust SDK behavior for streaming reconnects (see linked INT-34567).
comments:
[2026-03-12 10:14 - Support (Aisha Khan)]: Thanks for the reproduction and captures — we're investigating. Could you confirm which header name you set? (X-Idempotency-Key or Idempotency-Key?)

[2026-03-12 10:26 - Customer (Merriweather SRE)]: We set X-Idempotency-Key initially. Proxy logs show header trimmed to 8 bytes. We can reproduce consistently when traffic goes through our staging CDN.

[2026-03-12 12:03 - Support (Ben Park)]: We reproduced this with a local proxy that truncates headers. Short-term workaround: set a short idempotency token (<=8 bytes) to match proxy behavior or configure proxy to preserve full header. Long-term: we'll propose SDK change to prefer per-request UUIDs on reconnects for streaming.

[2026-03-13 09:05 - Engineering (Maya Lopez)]: Confirmed: ts-sdk streaming path will be updated to rotate the per-request idempotency token on reconnects. Also adding a normalized header name mapping (accept X-Idempotency-Key and Idempotency-Key) and code to warn when header appears truncated. Patch PRs opened: sdk-ts#201, sdk-python#482, sdk-go#153.
resolution:
Workaround and mitigation:
1) Customer temporary workarounds tried:
   - Configure proxy to pass through the full idempotency header (preferred).
   - Set a custom short idempotency token that fits the proxy limit (not ideal; potential increased collision risk across global traffic).
   - Disable streaming convenience session-scoped idempotency and instead generate a fresh UUID per request on the client side.

2) Platform/SDK fixes planned:
   - TS SDK: rotate per-request idempotency token on stream reconnects and emit a warning when a configured idempotency header exceeds 32 bytes. (PR sdk-ts#201)
   - Python/Go SDKs: add header normalization and server-side dedupe helpers in guidance docs. (PRs linked above)
   - Support runbook will include proxy guidance to avoid truncation/normalization issues for idempotency headers.

Follow-ups:
- INT-34567 created: apply SDK changes, add e2e test that simulates header truncation + RST_STREAM.
- Support to coordinate with customer for staged rollout and confirm resolution in their staging CDN.

Status: Engineering patching in progress, customer applied proxy config change in staging and reports no duplicates after the change. Will close when SDK patch is released and customer confirms in prod.
next_steps:
- Engineering to complete SDK PRs and add e2e tests (INT-34567).
- Support to validate fix with customer once SDK patch available; request customer to test in staging by re-enabling CDN policy.
- Update public docs with idempotency header best-practices for HTTP/2 proxies.
- Consider server-side defensive behavior: treat truncated matches as probable retries and prefer safe at-most-once semantics for function confirmations if configured.
notes: This ticket highlights an operational class of issues where network intermediaries mutate headers expected by dedup logic. Recommend adding a short section to our docs about header preservation and header-length considerations for customers using HTTP/2 multiplexing proxies.
